Q1: N,N-Dimethyl-methanamine-N-oxide exhibits known environmental, oral, and dermal/eye hazards according to official GHS classifications (Tier 1), with additional inhalation hazards identified through an expanded perspective (Tier 2). However, its hazard profile for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR), endocrine disruption (EDC), and organ/systemic effects (OGN) remains largely unknown due to data deficiencies (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is not present on any lists of concern. It is, however, included on the EPA's "Substances added to Food" inventory, indicating that it is generally considered of low concern when used as a regulated food or color additive.
Q3: N,N-Dimethyl-methanamine-N-oxide is generally well-characterized, evidenced by its defined molecular formula (C3H9NO), "Small Molecule" classification, and over 7,200 scientific references—well above the median for similar chemicals. Despite this, there are still significant data gaps concerning its potential carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, endocrine disruption, and organ/systemic effects.
